expect_nodes.name: mytool
expect_nodes.note: `subprocess.run(["mytool", "sync"], check=True)` invokes the tool. Extracted since A13.4: cli.rs scan_argv reads the LIST form (the only form that works without shell=True) and keys the node on argv[0], the binary; the args ride on the node's argv CODE cell. Before A13.4 extract_quoted() demanded a quote immediately after the pattern and this yielded nothing.

expect_edges.note: INTENDED: invocation -> declaration. EXPECTED to miss — the invocation now exists (A13.4), but the binary `mytool` is declared only in pyproject.toml [project.scripts], which nothing reads (LA.20), so there is no `cli:mytool` to pair with. The subcommand pass pairs `cli_invoke:mytool -> cli:sync` (Weak) instead, which this key does not assert.

forbid.name: sync
forbid.note: precision: the subcommand argument must never be minted as a separate invoked tool

note: ZERO-EVERYWHERE PROBE (A15.11), and a sharply actionable one. Baseline 2026-09-16 on the installed 0.4.18 wheel: 6 nodes / 3 edges, CLI_INVOCATION 0. The gap is one line: cli.rs INVOCATION_PATTERNS matches `subprocess.run(` and then demands a quote, so the canonical Python argv-list call is invisible. cli.rs's own unit test names this — it binds the list form to `_array_form` and asserts on the string form instead. A13.4 closed that gap (scan_argv reads the list form; the unit test now pins it); what still misses is the binary declaration in pyproject.toml (LA.20).
